report:
Reviewed the entire transaction_isolation claim, all seven associated implementation entries and both test entries. Captured the inference design, transaction/variable-identity RFD and staged-obligation dependency. Source inspection only; no behavioral tests rerun and no source changes.

The claim requires child-version isolation for potentially partial operations, exclusive-leaf atomic success and discard on failure/cancellation covering equalities, bounds, universes, wakes, tasks and staged obligations. unify.rs try_probe owns one child for its operation, rebuilds/collapses after success and discards after error. egraph.rs collapse_into validates direct parent, exclusive child and leaf conditions, transfers equality/bound/domain/universe/dependency/work/wake state, reowns variables and removes the child; discard clears every removed subtree state. version.rs freezes non-leaf parents against mutation and tombstones removed identities, preventing a removed child's ownership from becoming live through index reuse. These mechanisms also enforce the RFD distinction between read-only ancestor visibility and leaf writes.

boundary.rs apply_query_response imports and validates a complete response inside a caller child, collapsing only after all entries succeed and discarding on application error. infer_ctx.rs publishes explicitly staged obligation environments only after the caller has chosen to publish; the captured StagedObligationBatch is owned data with no automatic registry effect on drop. prove.rs solve_trait_frame gives each candidate a fresh instantiated proof state and child, extracts a canonical answer and discards the child; candidate states are never merged directly into the requester. runtime.rs ScopedTasks::cancel_all drops stored futures, resets live count and clears its queue, and Drop invokes cancellation. Since candidate futures own their independent proof states, cancellation drops their pending state instead of publishing it. The proof frame cancels remaining candidate tasks once its accepted unconditional answer permits this. These account for the cancellation and staged-publication paths without treating future cancellation as a root egraph commit.

The ordinary incompatible_transitive_domain_union_rolls_back test first commits Any/Integer, then attempts a conflicting union with Float. It requires DomainConflict with the correct Integer/Float domains, unchanged representatives of both classes, retained Integer domain and unchanged root semantic revision. Its local helpers allocate real egraph variables. This is meaningful transitive rollback coverage, but does not inspect discarded wake/task/obligation sets or exercise every failure class.

The inference_transaction_isolation TODO explicitly retains failed occurs/universe checks, multipart response imports, candidate matching/cancellation, unchanged parent/no-wake observations and sibling non-observation. Its prerequisite is completing that full transaction failure/cancellation matrix, including all state categories named in the claim. It has no assertions and remains visibly deferred. Existing unassociated helper tests in implementation files are not substituted for claim-associated evidence. Thus the one ordinary regression is not promoted to proof of every speculative operation, and all seven implementation associations and both evidence entries are accounted for. No concrete defect was identified in the inspected paths and no additional edits are requested.
